label: Luke 14:1
text: When he went into the house of one of the rulers of the Pharisees on a Sabbath to eat bread, they were watching him.

label: Luke 14:2
text: Behold, a certain man who had dropsy was in front of him.

label: Luke 14:3
text:
Jesus, answering, spoke to the lawyers and Pharisees, saying,
“Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?”

label: Luke 14:4
text:
But they were silent.
He took him, and healed him, and let him go.

label: Luke 14:5
text:
He answered them,
“Which of you, if your son
or an ox fell into a well, wouldn’t immediately pull him out on a Sabbath day?”

variants.reading: ὄνος ἢ βοῦς ('a donkey or an ox fell into a well')
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke' lists ὄνος ἢ βοῦς ('donkey or ox') for א (Sinaiticus), K, L, X, Π, Ψ, f1, f13, 33, 892, 1071, ℓ547; the WEB prints the reading υἱὸς ἢ βοῦς ('son or ox') of P45, P75 and B (Vaticanus).

variants.reading: πρόβατον ἢ βοῦς ('a sheep or an ox')
variants.note: The fetched variants article lists this reading for Codex Bezae (D); D is not a manuscript node of this graph, so attested_by is left empty.

label: Luke 14:6
text: They couldn’t answer him regarding these things.

label: Luke 14:7
text: He spoke a parable to those who were invited, when he noticed how they chose the best seats, and said to them,

label: Luke 14:8
text: “When you are invited by anyone to a marriage feast, don’t sit in the best seat, since perhaps someone more honorable than you might be invited by him,

label: Luke 14:9
text: and he who invited both of you would come and tell you, ‘Make room for this person.’ Then you would begin, with shame, to take the lowest place.

label: Luke 14:10
text: But when you are invited, go and sit in the lowest place, so that when he who invited you comes, he may tell you, ‘Friend, move up higher.’ Then you will be honored in the presence of all who sit at the table with you.

label: Luke 14:11
text: For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.”

label: Luke 14:12
text:
He also said to the one who had invited him,
“When you make a dinner or a supper, don’t call your friends, nor your brothers, nor your kinsmen, nor rich neighbors, or perhaps they might also return the favor, and pay you back.

label: Luke 14:13
text: But when you make a feast, ask the poor, the maimed, the lame, or the blind;

label: Luke 14:14
text: and you will be blessed, because they don’t have the resources to repay you. For you will be repaid in the resurrection of the righteous.”

label: Luke 14:15
text: When one of those who sat at the table with him heard these things, he said to him, “Blessed is he who will feast in God’s Kingdom!”

label: Luke 14:16
text:
But he said to him,
“A certain man made a great supper, and he invited many people.

label: Luke 14:17
text: He sent out his servant at supper time to tell those who were invited, ‘Come, for everything is ready now.’

label: Luke 14:18
text:
They all as one began to make excuses.
“The first said to him, ‘I have bought a field, and I must go and see it. Please have me excused.’

label: Luke 14:19
text: “Another said, ‘I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I must go try them out. Please have me excused.’

label: Luke 14:20
text: “Another said, ‘I have married a wife, and therefore I can’t come.’

label: Luke 14:21
text: “That servant came, and told his lord these things. Then the master of the house, being angry, said to his servant, ‘Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in the poor, maimed, blind, and lame.’

label: Luke 14:22
text: “The servant said, ‘Lord, it is done as you commanded, and there is still room.’

label: Luke 14:23
text: “The lord said to the servant, ‘Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled.

label: Luke 14:24
text: For I tell you that none of those men who were invited will taste of my supper.’”

label: Luke 14:25
text: Now great multitudes were going with him. He turned and said to them,

label: Luke 14:26
text:
“If anyone comes to me, and doesn’t disregard
his own father, mother, wife, children, brothers, and sisters, yes, and his own life also, he can’t be my disciple.

label: Luke 14:27
text: Whoever doesn’t bear his own cross, and come after me, can’t be my disciple.

label: Luke 14:28
text: For which of you, desiring to build a tower, doesn’t first sit down and count the cost, to see if he has enough to complete it?

label: Luke 14:29
text: Or perhaps, when he has laid a foundation, and is not able to finish, everyone who sees begins to mock him,

label: Luke 14:30
text: saying, ‘This man began to build, and wasn’t able to finish.’

label: Luke 14:31
text: Or what king, as he goes to encounter another king in war, will not sit down first and consider whether he is able with ten thousand to meet him who comes against him with twenty thousand?

label: Luke 14:32
text: Or else, while the other is yet a great way off, he sends an envoy, and asks for conditions of peace.

label: Luke 14:33
text: So therefore whoever of you who doesn’t renounce all that he has, he can’t be my disciple.

label: Luke 14:34
text: Salt is good, but if the salt becomes flat and tasteless, with what do you season it?

label: Luke 14:35
text: It is fit neither for the soil nor for the manure pile. It is thrown out. He who has ears to hear, let him hear.”

statement: One of the rulers of the Pharisees hosted Jesus for a meal in his house on a Sabbath, and those present were watching him.
label: A Sabbath meal in a ruler of the Pharisees' house

statement: Dropsy (fluid retention) was a recognized, serious illness in the ancient Mediterranean world, known to the Hippocratic corpus centuries before Luke.
label: Dropsy a recognized ancient illness

statement: At the Sabbath meal a man who had dropsy stood in front of Jesus, and Jesus took him, healed him, and let him go.
label: The man with dropsy healed on the Sabbath

statement: Guests invited to a marriage feast chose the best seats for themselves; banquet seating was ranked, with a best seat that could be reassigned and a lowest place to which a guest could be moved up.
label: Choosing the best seats at a feast

statement: A host giving a dinner or supper was urged to invite the poor, the maimed, the lame and the blind, who do not have the resources to repay him.
label: Inviting the poor who cannot repay

statement: Invited guests excused themselves from a great supper: one had bought a field and must see it, one had bought five yoke of oxen and must try them, one had married a wife.
label: Invited guests making excuses

statement: When the invited guests refused, the master of the house sent his servant into the streets and lanes of the city to bring in the poor, maimed, blind and lame, and then out into the highways and hedges, compelling them to come in.
label: Bringing in the poor from streets and lanes

statement: Building a tower was a major expense: a man intending one would first sit down and count the cost, and a man who laid a foundation and could not finish was mocked by all who saw it.
label: Counting the cost of building a tower

statement: A king going to encounter another king in war would first sit down and consider whether ten thousand could meet twenty thousand, and if not, send an envoy while the other was far off to ask for conditions of peace.
label: A king deliberating before a war he might lose
Herod's citadel towers at Jerusalem (Phasael, Hippicus, Mariamne; the 'Tower of David')
periods: Herod's three towers built late 1st century BCE on the Hasmonean western hill fortifications; the citadel rebuilt in later periods

author: Hippocrates (putative)

label: Deuteronomy 20:5-7 (exemptions from battle: new house, vineyard, new wife)
author: Deuteronomy

label: Wikisource: Hippocrates, The Book of Prognostics (F. Adams translation)
title: The Book of Prognostics (Hippocrates), Wikisource
excerpt: All dropsies arising from acute diseases are bad; for they do not remove the fever, and are very painful and fatal. The most of them commence from the flanks and loins, but some from the liver;

label: Wikipedia: Herodium (Herod's triclinium and banquet halls)
title: Herodium (triclinium and banquet halls)
excerpt: During the First Jewish–Roman War (66–73 CE), Herodium was held by Jewish rebels. At some point during the revolt, the fort's defenders transformed Herod's triclinium into a synagogue.

label: Wikipedia: Tower of David (Herod's three towers, Phasael 44 m)
title: Tower of David (Herod's towers)
excerpt: Herod named the tallest of the towers, 44 metres (144 ft) in height, Phasael, in memory of his brother who had committed suicide while in captivity.

label: Deuteronomy 20:5-7 (WEB, bible-api)
title: Deuteronomy 20:5-7 (WEB)
excerpt: What man is there who has built a new house, and has not dedicated it? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the battle, and another man dedicate it.

label: Sabbath rescue: a son or an ox out of a well
statement: Jesus argued that a man would immediately pull his son or his ox out of a well on the Sabbath day - Sabbath rescue of a child or animal was accepted practice (Luke's example; Matthew 12:11 has one sheep out of a pit).

label: A man's great supper; servant sent to call the invited
statement: A certain man who made a great supper sent his servant at supper time to tell those who were invited, 'Come, for everything is ready now' (Luke's host is a man, not Matthew's king giving a marriage feast for his son).
